Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — HelixAI is excited about Redwood's latency and tooling. We're trying to model an initial 12-month commitment and need clarity on two things before we take this to procurement:

1) Can you outline how per-token discounts apply if our traffic is split across US, EU, and APAC? We expect roughly 55% US, 30% EU, 15% APAC but some months will spike in APAC.
2) We want a commit slab structure (monthly token buckets) but with a predictable burst policy for occasional cross-region spikes. Is burst billed at retail, or is there a discounted overage tier?

Budgeting is tight; if there are simple examples (3-tier commit: 1M/5M/20M tokens) that show unit pricing per region + overage rules that would help.

Can you loop in billing/procurement contact or send a short proposal we can hand to our procurement team?

Hi Emma — great to hear from you and glad Helix liked the demo. Short answers up front: yes, we support region-aware unit pricing and we can put a burst buffer in the commitment with a capped discounted overage.

I'll sketch the high level here and attach a formal slab proposal after looping in Neha (billing) and Vivek (pricing lead) for approvals. Example (illustrative):
- Commit tiers (hosted, per-month buckets): 1M / 5M / 20M tokens
- Base unit price (US): $0.0008/token at 1M, $0.0006/token at 5M, $0.00045/token at 20M
- EU/EU regulated region uplift: +8% on unit price (higher infra cost & data handling)
- APAC uplift: +12% (regional egress & regional infra premium)
- Cross-region weighting: we bill tokens where they execute; if you want a blended rate we can offer a blended bucket at a negotiated uplift/discount.
- Burst policy option: reserve a 20% burst buffer on top of committed bucket billed at a pre-agreed overage rate (e.g., 1.5x base unit) up to a monthly cap. Above cap: retail overage.

I'll put Neha on thread to formalize numbers and add a spreadsheet. Quick question: do you need separate billing for EU data (entity vs. parent)? If so, we can provision split invoices.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Emma — copying Vivek and Laura for pricing and billing detail. I've attached a draft slab proposal (Redwood_Hosted_Pricing_Slab_Proposal.xlsx) and a short SLA addendum that spells out burst behavior and invoice treatment. Highlights from the spreadsheet: 

- Three commit tiers (monthly): 1M / 5M / 20M tokens. The sheet shows net unit prices after standard volume discount.
- Regional uplifts are additive to the unit price. We show the effective blended price for your 55/30/15 split and an alternate blended price for a hypothetical 40/30/30 split (to capture APAC spikes).
- Burst buffer: customers can pre-purchase a 10%, 20%, or 30% burst reserve at a fixed overage multiplier (1.35x / 1.25x / 1.15x respectively). Pre-purchased burst is cheaper than retail overage and is consumed before retail billing.
- Month-end reconciliation: if total monthly usage exceeds committed + pre-purchased burst, overage invoices apply at the retail rate. We include rolling credits for sustained underutilization (quarterly true-up) if you commit at 12 months.

We can also support split invoices (EU entity) and report token-level usage by region daily into your S3 endpoint for reconciliation.

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Pricing_Slab_Proposal.xlsx; SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf

Next steps: Rafael / Emma — let us know which commit tier you want modeled and whether you prefer a pre-purchased burst reserve or a capped pay-as-you-go burst. I'll produce a single-page summary for your procurement team.

Best,

Emma — quick note from pricing strategy perspective. Two pragmatic options that often work well for startups with variable region mixes: 

1) Blended global commit (single monthly bucket) — simplest for forecasting. We estimate an effective blended unit price given your expected split (we used 55/30/15). With a 12-month 5M/month commit we can offer an additional 3% strategic discount if you agree to a 20% pre-purchased burst buffer.

2) Regional pinning (separate buckets per region) — recommended if you need EU data residency billing separation or want to bus separate legal entities; more complex but gives you control over regional spend. Small administrative fee for maintaining multiple buckets.

On overages: recommend the pre-purchased burst model — lower unit economics for spikes and predictable spend. If you prefer flexibility, we can set a soft cap that triggers automated notification and a 24-hour automatic fallback to a lower-cost model (e.g., smaller local model) to avoid surprising invoices.

If Helix can share a 3-month sample of token distribution we can run the exact blended numbers and the impact of different burst sizes. Rafael — can you coordinate getting that sample?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercials, Redwood Inference
